back: If $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ and $f(a)f(b) < 0$, then $f(x) = 0$ has a root in $(a, b)$.
No sign change does not mean no root (even numbers of roots, touching the axis); a sign change at an asymptote is not a root.
Write the equation as $g(x) = h(x)$ and sketch both curves: intersections are roots.
$x_{n+1} = F(x_n)$; if it converges to $\alpha$, then $\alpha = F(\alpha)$.
To show α = 1.935 to 3 d.p., show a sign change between 1.9345 and 1.9355.
Iteration converges near $\alpha$ if $|F'(\alpha)| < 1$ and diverges if $|F'(\alpha)| > 1$.
$0 < F'(\alpha) < 1$: iterates approach from one side (staircase). $-1 < F'(\alpha) < 0$: they alternate sides (cobweb).
